scenarios.title: The Post-School Stall
scenarios.context: Teen arrives home exhausted. Parent wants to discuss a missing assignment.
scenarios.pilot: Running on fumes. Social battery dead, brain foggy.
scenarios.groundControl: Got an email from teacher, anxious to fix the problem.

crash.parent: Why didn't you turn in your history paper? You always do this.
crash.teen: Leave me alone! I just got home, why are you always on my case?
crash.outcome: System Overload. Both vehicles sustain damage.

optimization.parent: I see your State gauge is Amber right now. I have a Direction question about history, but I'll park it until you've had time to refuel.
optimization.teen: Copy that. My system is lagging. Give me a 30-minute reset, and then we can look at it.
optimization.outcome: Collision Avoided. Capacity restored before demands made.

scenarios.title: The Grade Drop
scenarios.context: Parent discovers teen's grades have dropped significantly this semester.
scenarios.pilot: Already feeling like a failure. Dreading this conversation.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried about teen's future. Feeling like you've failed as a parent.

crash.parent: A D in math?! What have you been doing all semester? No more phone until this is fixed!
crash.teen: I tried! You don't understand how hard it is! I'm not smart like you think!
crash.outcome: Shame spiral activated. Teen shuts down, problem gets worse.

optimization.parent: I noticed the math grade dropped. Before we talk solutions, I want to understand what's been happening in your system. What's your read on it?
optimization.teen: I don't know... I got lost after chapter 3 and was too embarrassed to ask for help.
optimization.outcome: Root cause identified. Now we can actually solve it together.

scenarios.title: The Homework Battle
scenarios.context: Teen hasn't started homework. Parent has reminded them three times.
scenarios.pilot: Planning to do it later. Feeling micromanaged.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried they'll stay up too late again. Pattern repeating.

crash.parent: I've told you THREE times! Start your homework NOW!
crash.teen: FINE! God, you never trust me to do anything!
crash.outcome: Homework done with resentment. Relationship damaged.

optimization.parent: I notice homework isn't started yet. What's your flight plan for tonight?
optimization.teen: I'm gonna start at 7 after I decompress a bit.
optimization.parent: Works for me. I'll check in at 7 to see if you need any support.
optimization.outcome: Autonomy respected. Clear agreement made.

scenarios.title: The Phone at Dinner
scenarios.context: Teen is scrolling during family dinner. Parent is frustrated.
scenarios.pilot: Friends are texting about drama. Feels urgent.
scenarios.groundControl: Feels disrespected. Misses real conversation.

crash.parent: Put that phone away RIGHT NOW! How many times do I have to tell you?
crash.teen: *eye roll* It's important!
crash.outcome: Tense dinner. No real connection. Same fight tomorrow.

optimization.parent: Hey, I'm noticing the phone is pulling you away. Something going on?
optimization.teen: Friend drama. Can I just send one text then put it away?
optimization.parent: One text, then phone in the basket. Deal?
optimization.outcome: Need acknowledged. Boundary maintained. Dinner saved.

scenarios.title: The Late Night Gaming
scenarios.context: It's 1am. Parent discovers teen still gaming.
scenarios.pilot: In the middle of a match with friends. Finally unwinding.
scenarios.groundControl: Has school tomorrow. This keeps happening.

crash.parent: It's 1am! Turn that off NOW! You're going to be a zombie tomorrow!
crash.teen: I can't just quit in the middle! You don't understand!
crash.outcome: Forced shutdown. Resentment. Same thing next week.

optimization.parent: Hey. It's past 1am. I get you're in a game — how much longer to finish this match?
optimization.teen: Like 10 more minutes.
optimization.parent: Okay. Finish this match, then we need to talk about a sustainable gaming schedule tomorrow. Your system needs sleep to function.
optimization.outcome: Dignity preserved. Real conversation scheduled.

scenarios.title: The Social Media Discovery
scenarios.context: Parent saw concerning content on teen's social media.
scenarios.pilot: Feels like privacy was violated. Embarrassed.
scenarios.groundControl: Scared about what they saw. Wants to protect.

crash.parent: What is THIS? Who are you talking to? I'm taking your phone!
crash.teen: You went through my stuff?! I can't trust you!
crash.outcome: Trust shattered both ways. No actual safety addressed.

optimization.parent: I saw something that worried me online. I'm not here to punish — I'm here because I care about your safety. Can we talk about it?
optimization.teen: How did you see that?
optimization.parent: That's fair to ask. Let's both be honest. I'm worried, not angry.
optimization.outcome: Safety concern addressed. Trust repair begins.

scenarios.title: The Party Request
scenarios.context: Teen wants to go to a party. Parent has concerns.
scenarios.pilot: Everyone's going. Doesn't want to be left out.
scenarios.groundControl: Doesn't know the parents. Worried about what happens at parties.

crash.parent: Absolutely not. I don't know those people. End of discussion.
crash.teen: You NEVER let me do anything! I hate this!
crash.outcome: Teen feels trapped. May sneak out. Trust broken.

optimization.parent: Tell me more about this party. I have some concerns, but I want to understand what's important to you about going.
optimization.teen: Everyone from the team is going. I don't want to be the only one who can't.
optimization.parent: Connection matters. Let's figure out what would make this work for both of us. What if I drove and picked up?
optimization.outcome: Compromise found. Safety addressed. Relationship intact.

scenarios.title: The New Friend Concern
scenarios.context: Teen is hanging out with someone parent doesn't like.
scenarios.pilot: This friend actually gets them. Feels judged by parent.
scenarios.groundControl: Sees red flags. Worried about influence.

crash.parent: I don't want you hanging out with Jake anymore. He's a bad influence.
crash.teen: You don't even know him! You judge everyone!
crash.outcome: Teen defends friend harder. Hides the friendship. Parent loses visibility.

optimization.parent: I've noticed you're spending a lot of time with Jake. I don't know him well — what do you like about him?
optimization.teen: He's funny and doesn't care what people think.
optimization.parent: That sounds freeing. I have some concerns I'd like to share when you're open to it. Not to control you — just to share my perspective.
optimization.outcome: Conversation stays open. Parent remains informed.

scenarios.title: The Dating Conversation
scenarios.context: Parent suspects teen is dating someone. Teen hasn't shared.
scenarios.pilot: Wants privacy. Worried about parent's reaction.
scenarios.groundControl: Feels left out. Wants to protect and guide.

crash.parent: Are you dating someone? Who is it? Why didn't you tell me?
crash.teen: It's none of your business!
crash.outcome: Wall goes up. Teen shares nothing. Parent worries more.

optimization.parent: I've noticed you seem happier lately. Whatever's going on, I'm here if you ever want to talk about relationship stuff. No pressure.
optimization.teen: ...maybe later.
optimization.parent: Door's open. I just want you to know I'm on your team.
optimization.outcome: Seed planted. Trust builds. Teen may share when ready.

scenarios.title: The Messy Room
scenarios.context: Teen's room is a disaster. Parent has asked many times.
scenarios.pilot: Knows where everything is. Doesn't see the problem.
scenarios.groundControl: Stressed by the mess. Feels disrespected.

crash.parent: This room is DISGUSTING! Clean it NOW or no friends this weekend!
crash.teen: It's MY room! Why do you care so much?!
crash.outcome: Power struggle. Clean room but damaged relationship.

optimization.parent: I notice the room hasn't been cleaned. What's your plan? I need it done before the weekend.
optimization.teen: I'll do it Saturday morning.
optimization.parent: Works for me. If it's not done by noon Saturday, no plans until it is. Deal?
optimization.outcome: Clear expectation. Natural consequence. Teen's choice.

scenarios.title: The Forgotten Chore
scenarios.context: Teen forgot to do their one chore — again.
scenarios.pilot: Genuinely forgot. Feels bad but defensive.
scenarios.groundControl: Fed up with reminding. Feels like a nag.

crash.parent: You had ONE thing to do! I can't rely on you for anything!
crash.teen: I FORGOT, okay?! You act like I'm the worst person ever!
crash.outcome: Shame spiral. No solution. Will forget again.

optimization.parent: The dishes didn't get done. I know you didn't mean to forget. What's getting in the way of remembering?
optimization.teen: I don't know... I just forget.
optimization.parent: Would a phone reminder help? Or doing it right when you get home before anything else?
optimization.outcome: System problem gets system solution.

scenarios.title: The Curfew Push
scenarios.context: Teen wants a later curfew. Parent says no.
scenarios.pilot: Friends all have later curfews. Feels babied.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried about safety. Current curfew feels right.

crash.parent: 10pm is the rule. End of story.
crash.teen: That's so unfair! I'm not a little kid anymore!
crash.outcome: Resentment builds. Teen may start lying about whereabouts.

optimization.parent: I hear you want a later curfew. Let's talk about it. What time are you thinking, and why?
optimization.teen: 11pm. Everyone else stays out that late and nothing bad happens.
optimization.parent: Here's my concern: safety. What if we try 10:30 for a month and see how it goes? If you're home on time and check in, we can revisit.
optimization.outcome: Trust ladder. Teen earns more freedom through demonstrated responsibility.

scenarios.title: The Privacy Demand
scenarios.context: Teen demands more privacy. Parent wants to monitor.
scenarios.pilot: Feels constantly watched. Needs space.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried about what they don't know. Wants to protect.

crash.parent: While you live under my roof, I have the right to know everything!
crash.teen: I have NO privacy! This is like a prison!
crash.outcome: Teen hides everything. Parent knows nothing. Both unsafe.

optimization.parent: I hear you need more privacy, and that makes sense as you get older. I also have a need to know you're safe. Where's the middle ground?
optimization.teen: I don't know... just don't go through my stuff?
optimization.parent: I can respect that. In return, I need you to come to me if something serious is happening. Deal?
optimization.outcome: Mutual respect. Safety net intact.

scenarios.title: The Isolation
scenarios.context: Teen has been in their room for days. Barely talking.
scenarios.pilot: Overwhelmed. Doesn't have words for it. Wants to be alone.
scenarios.groundControl: Scared something is really wrong. Feels helpless.

crash.parent: What is WRONG with you?! Why are you hiding? Talk to me!
crash.teen: Nothing! Leave me alone!
crash.outcome: Wall goes higher. Parent panics more. No connection.

optimization.parent: Hey. I notice you've been in your room a lot. I'm not here to interrogate. Just wanted to drop off a snack and let you know I'm here if you want company. No talking required.
optimization.teen: ...thanks.
optimization.outcome: Pressure-free presence. Door stays open.

scenarios.title: The Anxiety Reveal
scenarios.context: Teen admits they've been feeling really anxious.
scenarios.pilot: Vulnerable. Scared of parent's reaction.
scenarios.groundControl: Wants to fix it. May minimize unintentionally.

crash.parent: Anxious about what? You have nothing to worry about! Just think positive!
crash.teen: You don't understand. Forget I said anything.
crash.outcome: Teen never shares again. Anxiety worsens in isolation.

optimization.parent: Thank you for telling me that. Anxiety is hard. I'm not going to try to fix it right away — I just want to understand. What does it feel like for you?
optimization.teen: Like... my chest is tight all the time. And my brain won't stop.
optimization.parent: That sounds exhausting. I'm glad you told me. Let's figure out some support together.
optimization.outcome: Teen feels heard. Professional help becomes possible.

scenarios.title: The Big Emotion
scenarios.context: Teen is having a meltdown over something that seems small.
scenarios.pilot: Overwhelmed. This was the last straw.
scenarios.groundControl: Confused by intensity. Wants it to stop.

crash.parent: You're crying over THAT? Come on, it's not a big deal!
crash.teen: *cries harder* You don't get it!
crash.outcome: Emotion dismissed. Teen feels alone. Shame about feelings.

optimization.parent: Whoa, this is hitting hard. I can see you're really upset. I'm right here.
optimization.teen: *still crying*
optimization.parent: You don't have to explain. Let's just breathe together for a sec.
optimization.outcome: Co-regulation. Emotion moves through. Connection strengthens.

scenarios.title: The Lie Discovered
scenarios.context: Parent catches teen in a lie about where they were.
scenarios.pilot: Got caught. Scared of consequences. Has reasons for lying.
scenarios.groundControl: Feels betrayed. Trust is shattered.

crash.parent: You LIED to me! I can never trust you again! You're grounded for a month!
crash.teen: I lied because you never let me do anything!
crash.outcome: Punishment without understanding. Teen lies better next time.

optimization.parent: I found out you weren't where you said you'd be. I'm hurt, and we need to talk about this. But first — help me understand why you felt you couldn't tell me the truth.
optimization.teen: ...because you would have said no.
optimization.parent: So the lie felt safer than the conversation. That tells me we need to work on how we negotiate. The lie still has consequences, but I hear you.
optimization.outcome: Root cause addressed. Consequences AND repair.

scenarios.title: The Silent Treatment
scenarios.context: After an argument, teen won't speak to parent.
scenarios.pilot: Too angry to talk. Needs space to cool down.
scenarios.groundControl: Wants resolution. Silence feels like punishment.

crash.parent: Don't you ignore me! We're going to talk about this RIGHT NOW!
crash.teen: *silence*
crash.outcome: Escalation. Both dig in. Days of tension.

optimization.parent: I can see you're not ready to talk, and that's okay. I'll give you space. When you're ready, I'm here. No ambush.
optimization.teen: *nods slightly*
optimization.outcome: Space given. Teen comes back when regulated.

scenarios.title: The Attitude
scenarios.context: Teen is being short and snappy with everything parent says.
scenarios.pilot: Bad day. Taking it out on safe people.
scenarios.groundControl: Feels disrespected. Patience running thin.

crash.parent: Don't you take that tone with me! I'm your parent!
crash.teen: Whatever.
crash.outcome: Power struggle. Attitude continues. Everyone's day ruined.

optimization.parent: Okay, I'm noticing some edge in your responses. Bad day, or is something going on with us?
optimization.teen: ...I don't know. Just a bad day I guess.
optimization.parent: Got it. I'll give you some space. Let me know if you want to vent later.
optimization.outcome: De-escalation. Teen feels seen. Attitude softens.

scenarios.title: The Money Ask
scenarios.context: Teen wants money for something parent thinks is unnecessary.
scenarios.pilot: Really wants it. All their friends have it.
scenarios.groundControl: Thinks it's a waste. Money is tight.

crash.parent: Absolutely not! That's a waste of money! You don't need that!
crash.teen: You never get me anything! You don't understand!
crash.outcome: Teen feels dismissed. Resentment about money builds.

optimization.parent: Tell me more about why this matters to you.
optimization.teen: Everyone has one. I feel left out.
optimization.parent: I hear that. Here's the deal: I won't buy it, but if you save half, I'll match it. Or we can brainstorm ways you could earn it.
optimization.outcome: Value of money taught. Teen has agency. Goal achieved together.

scenarios.title: The Job Debate
scenarios.context: Teen wants a part-time job. Parent worried about school.
scenarios.pilot: Wants independence and own money.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried grades will slip. Teen already busy.

crash.parent: No job until you graduate. School is your job.
crash.teen: But I want my own money! You control everything!
crash.outcome: Teen feels trapped. May get job and hide it.

optimization.parent: I think wanting your own money is mature. My concern is your bandwidth. How would you balance school?
optimization.teen: I'd only work weekends. Like 10 hours max.
optimization.parent: Let's try it for one grading period. If grades stay up, we're good. If they drop, we reassess. Fair?
optimization.outcome: Trial period. Teen proves responsibility. Win-win.

scenarios.title: The College Pressure
scenarios.context: Teen isn't sure they want to go to college. Parent assumes they will.
scenarios.pilot: Doesn't know what they want. Feels pressured.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried about teen's future. College seems essential.

crash.parent: Of course you're going to college! That's not up for debate!
crash.teen: Maybe I don't want to! Why does everyone assume?!
crash.outcome: Teen feels unheard. May comply resentfully or rebel entirely.

optimization.parent: I realized I've been assuming college is the plan. Is that what you want? I'd love to hear what you're actually thinking about for your future.
optimization.teen: I don't know... maybe something with my hands? Trade school?
optimization.parent: That's a valid path. Let's explore options together. What matters most to me is that you have a plan, not that it looks a certain way.
optimization.outcome: Teen feels heard. Explores options authentically.

scenarios.title: The Career Dream
scenarios.context: Teen shares a career dream parent thinks is unrealistic.
scenarios.pilot: Excited to share. Wants parent's support.
scenarios.groundControl: Worried teen is being unrealistic. Wants to protect from failure.

crash.parent: A YouTuber? That's not a real career. You need a backup plan.
crash.teen: You never believe in me! Forget I said anything!
crash.outcome: Dream crushed. Teen stops sharing aspirations.

optimization.parent: Tell me more about what draws you to that. What would your life look like if it worked out?
optimization.teen: I love creating stuff. And some people actually make it!
optimization.parent: I can see the passion. What if we research together what it actually takes? I want to support you with eyes wide open.
optimization.outcome: Dream respected. Reality explored together.

scenarios.title: The Sibling Fight
scenarios.context: Siblings are fighting. Both want parent to take their side.
scenarios.pilot: Feels like sibling always gets away with things.
scenarios.groundControl: Exhausted by constant fighting. Wants peace.

crash.parent: Stop fighting! You're older, you should know better!
crash.teen: Why am I always the one in trouble?! They started it!
crash.outcome: Older child resentful. Fighting continues.

optimization.parent: Both of you, separate corners for 5 minutes. Then we'll have a mediation where each person gets to share without interruption.
optimization.teen: Fine.
optimization.parent: [After 5 min] Okay, Teen A, what happened from your perspective? Teen B, just listen...
optimization.outcome: Both heard. Conflict resolution modeled.

scenarios.title: The Divorce Adjustment
scenarios.context: Teen is struggling with parents' divorce.
scenarios.pilot: Grieving. Angry. Caught in the middle.
scenarios.groundControl: Also struggling. May accidentally burden teen.

crash.parent: Stop being so dramatic. Lots of kids have divorced parents. You'll adjust.
crash.teen: You don't care how I feel! You only care about yourself!
crash.outcome: Teen's grief invalidated. Acting out increases.

optimization.parent: I know this divorce has been hard on you. Your feelings about it are valid — the anger, the sadness, all of it. How are you doing today?
optimization.teen: I hate going back and forth. I hate that everything changed.
optimization.parent: I hate that for you too. This wasn't the plan. What would make the back and forth easier?
optimization.outcome: Grief witnessed. Practical solutions explored.

scenarios.title: The Step-Parent Tension
scenarios.context: Teen resists new step-parent's authority.
scenarios.pilot: Didn't ask for this. Feels loyalty to other parent.
scenarios.groundControl: Wants family to blend. Frustrated by resistance.

crash.parent: You WILL respect [step-parent]! They're part of this family now!
crash.teen: They're not my real parent and they never will be!
crash.outcome: Resistance hardens. Step-parent relationship damaged.

optimization.parent: I know having [step-parent] around is an adjustment. No one's asking you to replace anyone. It's okay if it takes time. What would help this feel less weird?
optimization.teen: I don't know... just don't force it, I guess.
optimization.parent: Fair. We'll take it slow. Your relationship with them is yours to figure out.
optimization.outcome: Pressure removed. Natural relationship can develop.

scenarios.title: The Extracurricular Quit
scenarios.context: Teen wants to quit an activity they've done for years.
scenarios.pilot: Burned out. Doesn't enjoy it anymore.
scenarios.groundControl: Invested time and money. Worried about quitting pattern.

crash.parent: You can't quit! You've put in years! What about the scholarship potential?
crash.teen: I hate it! You care more about the activity than me!
crash.outcome: Teen continues resentfully or quits explosively.

optimization.parent: I hear you want to quit. That's a big decision. Help me understand what changed.
optimization.teen: It used to be fun. Now it's just pressure and I dread it.
optimization.parent: That's important information. Let's talk about whether this is burnout that needs a break, or genuinely being done. Both are okay.
optimization.outcome: Thoughtful decision made together.

scenarios.title: The Comparison Spiral
scenarios.context: Teen is comparing themselves negatively to peers.
scenarios.pilot: Feeling not good enough. Everyone else seems to have it together.
scenarios.groundControl: Wants teen to see their worth. May accidentally dismiss.

crash.parent: Don't compare yourself to others! You're perfect just the way you are!
crash.teen: You have to say that. You're my parent.
crash.outcome: Feelings dismissed. Comparison continues in silence.

optimization.parent: Comparison is brutal. What specifically are you comparing?
optimization.teen: Everyone else seems smarter, more popular, better at everything.
optimization.parent: That sounds exhausting. You know what's interesting? I bet some of them look at you and think the same thing. What if we focused on what YOU value, not what everyone else has?
optimization.outcome: Feeling normalized. Redirect to values, not comparison.

scenarios.title: The Double Standard
scenarios.context: Teen calls out parent for not following their own rules.
scenarios.pilot: Frustrated by hypocrisy. Wants fairness.
scenarios.groundControl: Defensive. 'I'm the adult' instinct kicks in.

crash.parent: That's different! I'm an adult! Do as I say, not as I do!
crash.teen: That's so unfair! Rules don't count when it's you?
crash.outcome: Teen loses respect. Rules feel arbitrary.

optimization.parent: You know what, you're right. I have been doing that. Thanks for calling it out. I'll work on it.
optimization.teen: ...wait, really?
optimization.parent: Really. Fair is fair.
optimization.outcome: Respect earned. Modeling accountability.

scenarios.title: The Apology Needed
scenarios.context: Parent said something hurtful in the heat of the moment.
scenarios.pilot: Hurt. Waiting to see if parent will acknowledge it.
scenarios.groundControl: Knows they were wrong. Pride makes it hard.

crash.parent: *silence, pretends it didn't happen*
crash.teen: *distant, trust eroded*
crash.outcome: Wound festers. Teen learns not to expect accountability.

optimization.parent: Hey, I need to talk to you. Yesterday when I said [thing], that was wrong. I was frustrated but that's not an excuse. I'm sorry.
optimization.teen: ...it really hurt.
optimization.parent: I know. You didn't deserve that. I'll do better.
optimization.outcome: Repair modeled. Trust rebuilt. Teen learns healthy apologies.
